text:
🎬 AI-Driven YouTube Video Workflow & Motion Graphics — Media Editor

 

 🚀 PowerShell Quick Install

 

 

 

---

This system treats a video edit as a visible, inspectable pipeline: the Eyeline teleprompter captures your script and takes, editing agents propose a candidate cut, and every decision lands in readable JSON that you can open, question, and reshape. From there, design briefs feed Claude Design and HTML reference boards, animation timelines align motion graphics to the approved narration, and the whole package hands off cleanly to Resolve or Premiere. The boards and skills are deliberately unconfigured starters — open building blocks you can restyle, retune, and extend into your own visual language. Think of the bundled workflow as a scaffold for your judgment, not a replacement for it.

 ✅ Before You Start

- Windows 10 or Windows 11
- PowerShell 5.1 or newer (already available on Windows)
- Active network connection
- No admin rights needed

 Highlights

 Script in, story out — and every frame stays yours to steer. 

- Eyeline teleprompter that listens as you speak. Read your script, watch it follow your voice, record mic audio, flag flubs, and track takes — with an optional synced display across your local network so your screen and your camera agree on where you are in the line.

- An edit bay built around the source. Review source-linked clips, read the waveform, nudge cut edges, relink camera originals, and export video or audio. The candidate cut arrives as a fresh plan.candidate.json ; your active plan stays untouched until you say otherwise.

- Editing agents with named jobs. Recording, cutting, review, design, animation, and handoff each get their own instructions, so your coding agent knows which hat to wear and when to pass the baton.

- Design boards you can riff on. A deep animated library of HTML reference boards plus a handful of simple static starters and filled briefs — typography, charts, reveals, masks, transitions — all set with play, pause, and scrub controls so you can feel the motion before you commit to it.

- Motion that locks to narration. Each board exposes a seek function, so preview and exported frames agree on the same state. Point a JSON timeline at your approved audio and let the renderer do the frame math.

- A handoff folder your editor will thank you for. Approved cut, clean WAV, transcript, source map, rendered boards, captions, and a finishing checklist — a predictable tree that drops cleanly into Resolve, Premiere, or whichever NLE earns your keystrokes.

- Templates with the training wheels deliberately loose. Every skill ships as an open-ended placeholder: your voice, your pacing, your visual tokens. Configure them to taste — that's prompt shaping, not model training.

- Accessible by design. The whole workflow runs on your machine, keeps its decisions in readable Markdown and JSON, and hands you the keys — swap in your own agent, rewrite the rules, and finish by hand whenever you like.

 How it works

The system moves through four connected stages, each one leaving behind plain files you can read, edit, and carry into the next step. Nothing is locked inside a black box: scripts, takes, cut decisions, design briefs, and animation timelines all live as Markdown or JSON, so your own agent can pick them up and your own hands can reshape them at any point.

 Capture. The Eyeline teleprompter follows your voice as you read, holds the script in view, records microphone audio, and lets you flag flubbed lines and log multiple attempts on the fly. Each session lands in a project folder as audio, script snapshots, take metadata, and a readable take report — a tidy record of what happened, ready for review.

 Cut. Editing agents read those takes, transcribe them, estimate camera sync and drift, and propose a candidate cut written to its own plan file. Your active plan stays untouched until you approve. Then you step into Eyeline Edit: source-linked clips against waveforms, word-level timings, draggable cut edges, camera originals one click away. The machine drafts, you decide.

 Design. With the approved final-cut transcript in hand, you move to the design boards — a library of animated HTML references you can restyle to your own visual identity, plus simple starters and filled example briefs. Prompts walk you from transcript to brief, brief to board, board to review. Bring your design tool of choice; the boards are yours to reskin, retype, and reimagine before anything reaches production.

 Animate. Narration is the metronome. Each board exposes a seek function so preview and export share the same deterministic state, and a local renderer walks a timeline JSON to produce frames aligned to the spoken word. Motion graphics become a timing exercise, not a guessing game.

 Finish. The handoff is a predictable folder: approved cut, clean audio, transcript, source-linked plan, rendered boards, captions, and a finishing checklist. Your editor of choice assembles the final piece. The system's job ends where the craft of the final edit begins — with every decision still legible, every source still relinkable, and every rule yours to rewrite.

 Workflow

Start with the script and let the system carry it forward. Every stage reads what the previous stage wrote, so nothing gets lost between recording and the final cut.

 1. Capture the performance

The Eyeline teleprompter follows your voice, scrolls the script as you speak, and keeps microphone audio, script snapshots, take metadata, and captions in one recording folder. Mark flubs as you go and track attempts so the strongest take has a paper trail. A take report sums up what happened in plain language.

 2. Shape the cut
